item.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Is a Bad Look for a AI Layoffs
item.description: We’ve all been there: Your WiFi is down and you need a human to fix it, but first you have to run the gauntlet of the cable company’s dimwitted AI robots to access one. Now imagine you’re a $4 trillion company and the entire planet needs your computer problems fixed, like, yesterday, but you’ve sacrificed a third of your human employees to AI.

item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Richard Posner Transformed American Law With Economic Thinking
item.description: Judge Richard Posner, who died this week at 87, was the godfather of what is known as the law and economics movement. In a career spanning half a century and some 50 books, 500 articles, and thousands of judicial opinions, he pursued a single organizing idea: The purpose of law, rightly understood, is not to do justice but to pursue economic efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: Why Won’t Congress Unlock Cheaper Electricity?
item.description: The giant infrastructure permitting bill currently hanging in the balance of a lame duck Congress covers a lot of ground, from pipelines to power grids. One of its unifying objectives is affordability — it’s right there in the title: the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA. Cutting red tape for new energy pathways can both reduce their cost and open up sources of cheaper supply to alleviate the growing burden of electricity bills.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Iran War: US Still Needs a Deal to End Conflict
item.description: Nearly nine months ago, the US abandoned nuclear talks with Iran in favor of massive military strikes, gambling that force would collapse the regime or at least elicit more concessions than negotiations could. It would be foolish to make the same blunder twice.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Florida Republicans Think They Built a Red Wall. Can It Last?
item.description: There’s a reason that Florida is now America’s largest red state, and it’s not the one given by Florida Governor Ron DeSantis. Although the failed presidential candidate took credit for breaking last week’s blue wave by putting a constitutional amendment on the ballot, a look at the data shows he’s wrong.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Nvidia's Huang Scandal Stirs Up Murk Around Trump and Money
item.description: Former Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s sexual liaisons and myriad corporate spins with irresponsibility and self-indulgence have sparked a host of useful conversations — about unquenchable appetites, marital vows, titanic divorce settlements, possible national security breaches, the price of technological innovation and the resiliency of global trade, among others.
item.dc:creator: Timothy L. O'Brien

item.title: Rockstar Chefs Don't Have to Be the Best Cooks
item.description: Popular culture throws around the word “chef” as if anyone who works in a restaurant kitchen is one. Not so. item.title: COP31: We’re Missing a Big Problem With 35-by-35 Electrification
item.description: Electrification is the big theme at this year’s United Nations climate change conference, known as COP31, now taking place in Antalya, Turkey. But despite efforts to unite attendees, a fight is already brewing over whether a pledge to speed the electricity transition should require the use of clean energy. It’s the wrong thing to bicker about. Instead, countries should worry more about what that electricity is powering.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Ferrari Is Planning for the Future of the Car
item.description: Ferrari NV is worth more on the stock market than the three giants of Europe’s autos industry — Volkswagen AG, Renault SA and Stellantis NV — combined. There’s a reason for that.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Ebhardt

item.title: Anthropic IPO: Amodei Is About to Be Seriously Tested
item.description: Anthropic PBC has benefited from the single-minded focus of a leader who doesn’t waver from his decisions. But that advantage could become a liability as it speeds toward an initial public offering in the middle of a febrile market, with the Nasdaq having fallen about 6% in the past month and the possible ouster of Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang sapping confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson
